rows.notes: The document is an FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper (guideline/field guide) synthesising previously reported experience and data from other work; it reports no own experiment, survey, data collection or model runs on the claim. The relevant statement (Section 7) that subsurface tile or trickle systems create the fewest hazards of microbial contamination of air, soils and plants, while sprinklers create the greatest, is an unsupported general assertion in a guideline text, not a result of the authors' own study. The case summaries in Section 8 (e.g. Savva et al. tomato/lemon trials in UAE, wastewater re-use schemes in California) are secondary reports of other studies and do not address microbial contamination under drip. Hence Q1 is no and all subsequent questions are no.
